subject: Urgent: latency + error-rate spike after v5.2 quant deploy
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@stellarnet.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@stellarnet.com>, support@stellarnet.com
Date: 2026-08-12 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: High p95 latency and 500s after your v5.2 quant deploy

Karthik —

We pushed the v5.2 model/quant profile yesterday (your note said safe rollout). Since ~02:00 UTC we've been seeing p95 jump from ~420ms to ~1.6s and a steady ~2% 500 error rate on the inference endpoint that powers our fraud-check flow. A subset of requests show repeated "KV cache mismatch" errors in logs (attached sample). This is causing timeouts in our payment pipeline and impacting conversion.

We rolled back client-side routing to the older model variant for a small percentage, which helped request success rate, but the latency remains high. Can you confirm whether any kernel/quant kernels shipped with v5.2 could change runtime memory pressure or change batch behavior? We need a quick mitigation plan and an ETA.

Attachments: perf-graphs-08-12.png, error-sample-logs.txt

— Amit
Principal Engineer, StellarNet

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@stellarnet.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 500s after your v5.2 quant deploy

Amit —

Thanks for the quick note and the logs. We're looking into it now. Quick context: v5.2 included a new int8 quant profile and a kernel rebind that can change memory layout for KV caching on certain sequence-length distributions. We haven't seen a consistent customer-facing p95 increase in staging, so this looks like a workload-specific interaction.

Immediate plan (steps we are executing now):
- Ops: pin your traffic to the v5.1 variant (we can set a routing rule for 90% -> v5.1 immediately).
- Runtime: collecting full KV cache traces and per-GPU tail-latency metrics (INF-9123).
- Performance: run a replay of your recent traffic profile against both v5.1 and v5.2 in a dedicated infra slice.

I'll pull Marissa to coordinate the customer call and Rishi will lead the perf replay. Expect a short update in ~60–90 minutes.

— Kar
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@stellarnet.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 500s after your v5.2 quant deploy

Amit —

We've applied a routing rule: 100% of new traffic for your fraud-check route is now on v5.1. You should see error-rate reduce within the next 5–10 minutes. We're still collecting traces for the affected requests and will share a diagnostic bundle.

Can you confirm whether your requests during the spike had atypical prompt lengths (long system messages or nested user context)? That would help us reproduce.

Proposed next steps for tomorrow's working session:
- Hour-long joint replay session (we'll bring perf and runtime engineers).
- If replay reproduces the latency, we will either: roll-forward a hotfix quant kernel or flip a quant profile back to the prior qconfig for your tenant.

Attachments: kvcache-dump-08-12.jsonl (sample)

— Marissa
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Amit Shah <amit@stellarnet.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@stellarnet.com>, ceo@stellarnet.com
Date: 2026-08-12 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p95 latency and 500s after your v5.2 quant deploy

Thanks — We see error rate drop to ~0.3% after routing back. p95 dropped a bit but remains ~1.1s (still above SLO for the fraud path). Priya is looping in the CTO/CEO since this has direct revenue impact; they want an exec-level troubleshooting note and the remediation path spelled out. Can you provide a short exec summary and a timeboxed remediation plan?

We can do the replay session tomorrow 10:00 AM ET.

— Amit

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@stellarnet.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive summary & remediation options (v5.2 quant profile impact)

Amit / Priya —

Executive summary (TL;DR): After v5.2's int8 quant profile rollout, StellarNet observed a p95 latency increase and a small spike in 500s tied to KV cache misalignment for a subset of long-context fraud-check requests. Rolling routing to v5.1 restored success rates; p95 improved but not fully to baseline. Root cause appears to be an interaction between the new qconfig memory layout and your request sequence-length distribution causing increased GPU memory churn and slower KV cache hits.

Impact: revenue-sensitive fraud path saw increased timeouts and slowed authorizations for ~2 hours at peak. No data-exfiltration; errors are runtime failures.

Options & timeline (pick one):
1) Immediate rollback (recommended if business impact is high): flip tenant to v5.1 globally. Ops ETA: 15 minutes for routing + 30 minutes to validate. Recovery risk: none.
2) Hotfix quant kernel (if you want to stay on v5.2): engineering builds a qfix that preserves the new model behavior but restores KV layout for your traffic. ETA: 48–72 hours (test + canary).
3) Profile-tuned fallback: keep v5.2 for most traffic, route heavy long-context flows to v5.1 via rule-based routing. ETA: 2–4 hours to configure and validate.

Immediate ask from StellarNet: please confirm which option you prefer. We're prepared to execute rollback within 15 minutes of confirmation. We'll run the replay tomorrow 10:00 AM ET to validate hotfix/profiling hypotheses and follow up with a postmortem.

Jira ticket: INF-9123 (link included). Diagnostic artifacts: s3://customer-artifacts/stellarnet/DEAL-4782/diagnostics/2026-08-12/ (logs and graphs attached).

— Kar
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
